A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LOM research. The complete main text and Appendices A–C are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, figures, tables, and proofs can be matched despite reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original LOM evaluations on D4RL and Fetch tasks, component-count sensitivity experiments, and synthetic action-distribution experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental outcomes in Tables 1–2, Figures 2–5, and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same mixture density network, hyper Q-function, greedy mode selection, and advantage-weighted imitation procedure. Algorithm 1 and the substantive learning objectives are unchanged; objective-notation cleanup does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 15 D4RL locomotion settings, FetchReach, FetchPush, FetchPickAndPlace, and the synthetic one-step MDP in Appendix A. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains OneStep, AWAC, CQL, TD3BC, LAPO, DMPO, WCGAN, and WCVAE. Table 2 retains BC, MDN, AWAC, WCGAN, and WCVAE; Appendix A also retains the same model comparisons.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, Fetch reward structures, normalized-score evaluation, Gaussian-component sweeps, and the architectures and hyperparameters in Table 3 remain unchanged. No evaluation protocol is introduced or revised.

E4.justification: The Fetch action-distribution study, component-count sensitivity analyses in Figures 3–4, and synthetic modelling comparison in Appendix A are retained with the same evidence. Figure relocation does not introduce another analysis.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions specify four random seeds and the same standard-deviation reporting practice. The reported uncertainty entries remain unchanged, with no additional statistical procedures or run information.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–2 and plotted results in Figures 2–5 match. The TD3BC walker2d-medium-expert entry remains 110.1; v2 merely removes a dangling plus-minus symbol without changing a value or uncertainty estimate.

T1.justification: The H-MDP definitions, Proposition 1, Theorems 1–3, and Appendix B proofs retain the same mathematical content. Section 3 and Equations 9–11 and 18 clean up objective-versus-optimizer notation without revising assumptions, arguments, or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-mode imitation, hyper-policies and hyper Q-functions, policy-improvement guarantees, and performance on multi-modal offline RL benchmarks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of action averaging, mode selection, and component-count sensitivity are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same concerns about hyper Q-function Bellman targets and the computational cost of identifying modes separately for each state.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same baseline objectives, network architectures, hyperparameters, and component-selection range. The code-access information is also unchanged; no implementation or reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prior offline RL and multi-modal modelling approaches are unchanged. Differences in citation punctuation and bibliography formatting do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar, spelling, terminology, and objective-notation corrections and changes heading and citation styles. It adds the ICLR publication header while retaining the section sequence, appendix organization, and almost all prose.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into the ICLR template, changing typography, spacing, and float placement. Figures 1 and 3 now sit beside wrapped text, Figure 3 is substantially smaller and appears below Figure 4, and Table 3 occupies a separate final page. Figure and table content is retained.

improvement.justification: The methods, experimental evidence, theoretical arguments, and reproducibility information are unchanged. Small wording and notation fixes provide editorial polish, while the new layout shrinks Figure 3 and separates Table 3 from its explanation. These presentation tradeoffs leave overall quality essentially unchanged.
